suppress.notes: CVE-2026-22816: Gradle dependency-resolution spoofing via lapsed domain names. Affects Gradle versions before 9.3.0. gradle-8.4.2.jar, gradle-api-8.4.2.jar, and gradle-settings-api-8.4.2.jar are build-tool JARs that are never bundled into the Android APK and are not present at app runtime. The vulnerability requires control over repository infrastructure during a build, which is a build-environment concern, not a shipped-app concern. See: https://github.com/gradle/gradle/security/advisories/GHSA-jgvh-hgmg-6wp5

CVE-2026-22865: Gradle dependency-resolution spoofing (variant of CVE-2026-22816). Same reasoning: gradle-8.4.2.jar and related Gradle JARs are build-tool artifacts only — never included in the Android APK. Not exploitable at app runtime. See: https://github.com/gradle/gradle/security/advisories/GHSA-jgvh-hgmg-6wp5

CVE-2024-7254: protobuf-java denial-of-service via recursive parsing. protobuf-java-3.22.3.jar appears in the Gradle cache because it is pulled in by build-time tooling (kotlin-gradle-plugin-idea-proto, AGP, etc.). The Android app itself depends only on protobuf-lite (the android-optimised variant), which is a separate artifact and is not affected by this CVE. See: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-735f-pc8j-v9w8

CVE-2023-44487: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset attack (CVE-2023-44487). This vulnerability affects HTTP/2 server implementations. The Android app is a pure HTTP client — it never listens for or accepts HTTP/2 connections. The gRPC jars (grpc-*-1.57.0.jar) are transitive dependencies pulled in by Firebase/Play Services for internal GCP communication; the app code does not directly open gRPC server sockets. Netty (4.1.93.Final) is likewise a transitive dependency of gRPC and is not exploitable via client-only use. See: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/security/advisories/GHSA-xpw8-rcwv-8f8p

CVE-2025-55163: Netty HTTP/2 CONTINUATION flood denial-of-service. Affects Netty server configurations. The app only uses Netty transitively through gRPC (Firebase/Firestore SDK) as a client. No server-side socket is opened by the app, so this server-side DoS vector is not reachable. See: https://github.com/netty/netty/security/advisories/GHSA-4g8c-wm8x-jfhw

CVE-2021-33813: jdom2 SSRF / unbounded entity expansion in XML parsing. jdom2-2.0.6.jar is used by Gradle's XML processing during the build and is not bundled into the Android APK. The app does not parse untrusted XML at runtime using jdom2. See: https://github.com/hunterhacker/jdom/issues/188

CVE-2023-31582: jose4j algorithm confusion / weak key acceptance. jose4j-0.7.0.jar is not a dependency of the Android app. It appears in the scan because it is a runtime dependency of the OWASP Dependency Check tool itself. The Gradle cache scan inadvertently picks up tool JARs alongside app JARs. See: https://github.com/openid/AppAuth-Android (jose4j is not used by the app)
CVE-2024-29371: jose4j signature validation bypass. Same reasoning as CVE-2023-31582: jose4j is an OWASP DC tool dependency scanned incidentally from the Gradle cache, not an app runtime dependency.
